**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil, "The Landmarks of Revelation") on surah 80, verses 37–41:**

﴿For every person among them on that Day, there will be a matter that occupies him.﴾ It preoccupies him away from the concerns of others.

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi related to us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi related to us; al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah informed me; Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman related to us; Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz related to us; Ibn Abi Uways related to us; my father related to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Ayyash, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Sawda, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be resurrected barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, the sweat having bridled them and reached the lobes of their ears." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, alas for our shame! Will some of us look at others?" He said: "People will be preoccupied. For every person among them on that Day, there will be a matter that occupies him." [[Narrated by al-Hakim, 2/514–515, who said: "This is a hadith whose chain is sound according to the conditions of Muslim." al-Suyuti, in al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/423, added its attribution to al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi. al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id, 10/333: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are the narrators of the sound (collection) except Muhammad ibn Ayyash, who is trustworthy." He also mentioned it in Majma' from the narration of al-Tabarani and said: its narrators are trustworthy. It is also attributed in Kanz to Ibn Mardawayh in al-Ba'th, 14/363.]]

﴿And faces on that Day will be radiant﴾ shining and bright.

﴿Laughing﴾ with joy, ﴿joyful﴾ delighted by what they have attained of the honour of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And faces on that Day will have upon them dust﴾ blackness and the gloom of grief [and sorrow] [[Omitted from manuscript "b".]] ﴿covered by darkness﴾ overtaken and enveloped by gloom and dimness. Ibn Abbas said: "It will be covered by humiliation." Ibn Zayd said: "The difference between al-ghabara (dust) and al-qatara (darkness) is that al-qatara is the dust that rises and reaches the sky, while al-ghabara is what remains low on the earth."
